notes: Every item with verify=true must be re-checked after each Union Budget and PFRDA/EPFO notification.
Returns and inflation are planning assumptions, not forecasts.
This pack contains no personal data and is safe to publish.

derived.name: fireCorpus
derived.label: FIRE corpus
derived.description: Sum of holdings counted toward FIRE, excluding emergency fund.

derived.name: monthlySurplus
derived.label: Uninvested monthly surplus
derived.description: takeHome − expenses − EMIs − money invested from take-home. PF isn't subtracted: it never reaches take-home.

assumptions.label: General inflation
assumptions.help: Long-run CPI assumption for household costs.

assumptions.label: Healthcare inflation
assumptions.help: Medical costs in India have historically risen faster than CPI.

assumptions.label: Education inflation
assumptions.help: School and college fees; typically above CPI.

assumptions.label: Portfolio return before FIRE
assumptions.help: Blended yearly return while you are still investing. The default is the weighted return of the rules pack's pre-FIRE allocation (65% equity, 25% debt, 7% gold, 3% cash).

assumptions.label: Portfolio return after FIRE
assumptions.help: Blended yearly return while you draw down. Lower than before FIRE because more of the corpus sits in debt and cash (the three-bucket approach).

assumptions.label: Yearly ups and downs before FIRE
assumptions.help: How much the portfolio's return typically swings in a year (standard deviation). Indian equity swings about 18–20%, debt 2–4%; a 65% equity mix is about 13%. Used for the 'chance your money lasts' simulation.

assumptions.label: Yearly ups and downs after FIRE
assumptions.help: Lower than before FIRE because less of the corpus is in equity.

assumptions.label: Annual income growth
assumptions.help: Drives EPF and other salary-linked contributions.

assumptions.label: Annual SIP step-up
assumptions.help: Yearly increase in SIP until FIRE.

assumptions.label: Plan until age
assumptions.help: The corpus must last until this age. 90–95 is prudent.

assumptions.label: Share of equity withdrawals that is gain
assumptions.help: Only the gain part of an equity sale is taxed. For money invested over 10+ years, about half of what you sell is gain.

assumptions.label: Rebalance band (absolute)
assumptions.help: Rebalance when a class drifts more than this many percentage points…

assumptions.label: Rebalance band (relative)
assumptions.help: …or more than this share of its own target (catches small classes).

assetClasses.label: Equity
assetClasses.help: Indian and international equity: index funds, active funds, stocks.

assetClasses.label: Debt
assetClasses.help: EPF, PPF, NPS debt, FDs, bonds, debt funds.

assetClasses.label: Gold
assetClasses.help: Gold ETFs/FoFs, SGBs. Physical jewellery is not counted.

assetClasses.label: Real estate / REIT
assetClasses.help: Listed REITs/InvITs and investment property (not your own home).

assetClasses.label: Cash
assetClasses.help: Liquid funds and savings kept for investing, not the emergency fund.

taxTreatments.label: Listed equity & equity-oriented funds
taxTreatments.summary: LTCG 12.5% above ₹1.25 lakh/yr exemption if held >12 months; STCG 20%.

taxTreatments.label: Debt funds bought on/after 1 Apr 2023
taxTreatments.summary: Gains taxed at slab rate regardless of holding period.

taxTreatments.label: Interest income (FD, RD, bonds, savings)
taxTreatments.summary: Interest taxed at slab rate as it accrues.

taxTreatments.label: Gold ETF / Gold FoF
taxTreatments.summary: LTCG 12.5% without indexation after 12 months (ETF) or 24 months (FoF); shorter holding at slab rate.

taxTreatments.label: Sovereign Gold Bond
taxTreatments.summary: Redemption at maturity tax-free; secondary-market sale taxed as LTCG 12.5% after 12 months. 2.5% interest taxed at slab.

taxTreatments.label: Exempt-Exempt-Exempt
taxTreatments.summary: Contribution, growth and withdrawal all tax-free (PPF, SSY).

taxTreatments.label: EPF / VPF
taxTreatments.summary: Withdrawal tax-free after 5 years' continuous service. Interest on employee contributions above ₹2.5 lakh/yr is taxable.

taxTreatments.label: NPS Tier-1
taxTreatments.summary: Lump sum at 60 tax-free; mandatory annuity portion; annuity income taxed at slab. Exit and annuity rules have been changing — confirm current PFRDA rules.

taxTreatments.label: REIT / InvIT units
taxTreatments.summary: Units: LTCG 12.5% after 12 months. Distributions: interest/dividend parts at slab, capital repayment part reduces cost.

taxTreatments.label: Investment property
taxTreatments.summary: LTCG 12.5% without indexation after 24 months; rent taxed at slab after 30% standard deduction.

taxTreatments.label: International funds / foreign stocks
taxTreatments.summary: Treatment depends on the fund structure and holding period; FoFs investing abroad are generally not equity-oriented.

taxTreatments.label: Traditional life insurance (endowment/money-back)
taxTreatments.summary: Maturity tax-free only within premium limits set in recent budgets; otherwise taxed. Check your policy.

instruments.label: EPF

access.note: Full withdrawal allowed after 2 months of unemployment; otherwise at 58.

instruments.help: Find the balance in the EPFO passbook / UMANG app.

access.note: 15-year lock-in from account opening; partial withdrawals from year 7; extendable in 5-year blocks.

instruments.label: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana

access.note: Earmarked for daughter's education/marriage; partial withdrawal at 18.

instruments.help: Usually better modelled as funding a goal than as FIRE corpus.

instruments.label: NPS Tier-1

access.note: Locked till 60 (limited partial withdrawals); part of the corpus must buy an annuity.

instruments.help: Mixed equity/debt. Mark as counting toward FIRE only if your FIRE age is 60+.

unlock.note: At 60, at least 40% must buy an annuity (pension); the rest can be taken tax-free. PFRDA has been revising exit rules; check the current limits.

access.note: ELSS has a 3-year lock-in per instalment.

instruments.label: Equity-oriented hybrid fund
instruments.help: Classed as equity for simplicity; split manually if you want precision.

access.note: Premature withdrawal usually allowed with a penalty.
Eligible from 60 (55 on retirement, conditions apply).

instruments.label: Sovereign Gold Bond

access.note: 8-year tenure; early redemption windows from year 5; tradable on exchanges.

instruments.help: No new tranches issued since early 2024 as far as known; existing bonds still count.

instruments.label: Investment property (not your home)
instruments.help: Count it only if you will actually sell it or rely on its rent (add rent under Incomes).

instruments.label: Endowment / money-back policy

access.note: Use surrender value today, not sum assured.

instruments.help: Enter the current surrender value. Premiums go under Expenses → Protection.

expenseCatalog.label: Rent
expenseCatalog.hint: Skip if you own your home.

expenseCatalog.label: Electricity
expenseCatalog.hint: Usually rises when home all day.

expenseCatalog.label: Vehicle insurance, service, parking
expenseCatalog.hint: Car replacement is a Goal, not an expense.

expenseCatalog.label: School fees
expenseCatalog.hint: Stops when the child finishes school.

expenseCatalog.label: Health insurance premium
expenseCatalog.hint: Employer cover ends at FIRE — budget for your own family floater.

expenseCatalog.label: Term insurance premium
expenseCatalog.hint: Stops when the policy term ends.

expenseCatalog.label: Endowment / ULIP premiums
expenseCatalog.hint: Treat as an expense until the policy ends.

expenseCatalog.label: Festivals, functions, gifts
expenseCatalog.hint: Diwali, Pongal, Onam, Eid, Christmas, weddings you attend…

expenseCatalog.label: Other (describe in comment)
expenseCatalog.hint: Anything city- or family-specific not listed above.

goalTemplates.label: Appliances, electronics, furniture
goalTemplates.hint: Fridge, AC, laptop, phones: a rough total every few years.

goalTemplates.label: Car purchase / replacement
goalTemplates.hint: Set 'Repeats every' for replacements, e.g. every 8 years.

inflowTemplates.label: Gratuity
inflowTemplates.hint: Paid when you leave after 5+ years: 15 days' last basic + DA for each year of service. Tax-free up to ₹25 lakh for private-sector employees.

inflowTemplates.label: Insurance maturity / survival benefit
inflowTemplates.hint: Endowment, money-back or guaranteed-income plans. Usually tax-free under Sec 10(10D) if premiums stay within the limits; check your policy.

inflowTemplates.label: Property sale
inflowTemplates.hint: Easier: add the property under Property and choose 'Sell'. That handles growth, costs and capital-gains tax. Use this only for a sale you don't want to list there.

inflowTemplates.label: Leave encashment / other exit benefit
inflowTemplates.hint: Paid when you leave your job.

inflowTemplates.label: Bonus, ESOP or RSU vesting
inflowTemplates.hint: Enter the amount after tax, or set the tax rate.

inflowTemplates.label: Inheritance or gift
inflowTemplates.hint: No inheritance tax in India; gifts from relatives are tax-free.

property.growthHint: Long-run residential prices in Indian cities have grown at roughly inflation to a little above it, with big differences by city and locality and long flat spells. Check your city in the RBI House Price Index or NHB RESIDEX, and your locality's recent sale prices, before using more than 5–6%.
property.asOf: LTCG 12.5% without indexation (Finance Act 2024); property bought before 23 Jul 2024 may choose 20% with indexation

healthCover.note: Indicative yearly premium for a ₹15 lakh family floater (two adults) by the elder's age, in today's money. Real quotes vary by insurer, city and health; get one and enter it.

incomeTax.note: Slab income after FIRE: interest and debt-fund gains, rent (after 30% standard deduction), pension. Equity gains are taxed separately at 12.5% above ₹1.25 lakh. The Sec 87A rebate doesn't apply to equity gains. Surcharge above ₹50 lakh income is ignored. Slabs are assumed to rise with inflation.

resolution.note: Detailed wins once the 'expenses' section is in sectionsDone.
Quick answer is optional; fallback splits out an assumed healthcare share.
Quick answer: money invested from take-home pay. PF (own + employer) is asked separately.

resolution.detailed: sum(holdings where instrument in [epf,vpf], monthlyContribution + employerMonthlyContribution)
resolution.note: Quick answer: PF deduction + employer PF from the payslip.

quick.title: Quick estimate
quick.intro: Nine questions, about two minutes. You'll get a first FIRE age with a confidence score; refine any section afterwards.

questions.help: Only your age is needed. It's saved as an approximate birth month so it stays correct when you come back next year, and it never leaves your device.

questions.prompt: At what age would you like to stop depending on a salary?
Until what age should your money last?
questions.help: Plan beyond the average. Life expectancy at birth in India is around 70–72, but people who reach their 40s in good health often live into their 80s, and many past 90. 90–95 is a prudent choice.
questions.impactHint: Each extra 5 years adds roughly 5–8% to the corpus you need.
Used to spot money left over each month that isn't invested yet.
questions.help: What reaches your bank account each month, after income tax and PF are deducted. Include your spouse's if you share expenses.

questions.prompt: Monthly household spending, excluding EMIs and investments?
questions.impactHint: The single biggest driver: ±10% here moves the corpus needed by ±10%.

questions.help: Assumed to end before FIRE unless you add loan details later.

questions.prompt: How much have you invested so far?
questions.help: Mutual funds, stocks, PPF, FDs, gold, and your PF balance (EPFO passbook or the UMANG app). Leave out your home, and NPS Tier-1 if you plan to stop before 60 (it's locked until then).

questions.prompt: How much do you invest each month from your take-home pay?
questions.help: Money that leaves your bank account: SIPs, PPF, RDs, VPF, your own NPS. Don't include your PF deduction here; that's the next question.
questions.impactHint: Only money you invest yourself. Your employer's share comes next.

questions.prompt: How much goes into your PF each month?
questions.help: From your payslip: your PF deduction plus your employer's PF contribution. It's taken out before your salary reaches you, so it isn't part of your take-home. Enter 0 if you don't have PF.
questions.impactHint: Employer money is still your money: it grows in your PF and counts toward FIRE.

refine.title: Break down your expenses
refine.intro: Line by line, monthly or annual. Anything not listed goes in 'Other' with a comment.

questions.impactHint: Separates essentials from lifestyle spending and applies post-FIRE changes like lower commuting.

refine.title: List your investments
refine.intro: One row per account or fund. Mark what you can actually use at your FIRE age.

refine.title: Life goals
refine.intro: Big one-off costs paid from your corpus: education, weddings, car, home.

questions.impactHint: A ₹25 lakh education goal 12 years out needs about ₹80 lakh at 10% inflation.

refine.title: Money coming in
refine.intro: Lump sums you expect: gratuity, insurance maturities, a property sale, an inheritance. Add a date and amount for each; payouts spread over several years can repeat yearly.

questions.prompt: Add money you expect to receive
questions.impactHint: Money received before FIRE is invested; money received later reduces what you need to have saved.

refine.title: Property
refine.intro: Homes and land aren't part of your FIRE corpus, but they matter: rent pays some bills, a sale can fund years of retirement, and costs continue while you own them.

questions.prompt: How many parents do you support financially?

questions.impactHint: A loan running past your FIRE age becomes a retirement expense.

questions.prompt: Family health cover you own (excluding employer cover)
Health insurance premium you'll pay after you stop working (a year, today's money)
questions.help: Employer cover ends when you stop working. Enter your current quote for a family floater of at least ₹15 lakh. Leave blank to use an estimate; enter 0 only if this is already in your monthly spending.

questions.prompt: Term policy ends at your age
Plan for money to last until age
Spending after FIRE compared with today
questions.help: For example 85% if you'll move to a cheaper city, 110% if you'll travel more. Leave blank for 100%. Applies on top of the per-category changes in Expenses.

questions.prompt: Part-time / consulting income after FIRE (monthly, today's ₹)
questions.help: Barista FIRE. Leave 0 for full FIRE.

refine.title: Assumptions
refine.intro: Sensible defaults are pre-filled. Change only if you have a reason.

questions.prompt: Review inflation, returns and tax assumptions
questions.help: Rendered as a table of rules-pack assumptions with editable overrides.

confidence.method: Each answer scores by source: exact 1.0, estimate 0.6, default 0.3, missing 0. Quick-pass answers count as 'estimate' for the sections they stand in for. Score = Σ(section weight × mean answer score) ÷ Σ(weights of visible sections) × 100. Range: rerun the engine with expenses +band and corpus −band (and vice versa) to show an earliest-FIRE-age range.

bands.label: Rough
bands.message: Ballpark only. Refine expenses and investments first.

bands.label: Solid
bands.message: Detailed enough to plan against. Revisit yearly.

tiers.label: Lean FIRE
tiers.description: Only categories marked essential. Needs the expenses section.

tiers.label: Standard FIRE
tiers.description: Your current lifestyle, adjusted for post-FIRE factors.

tiers.label: Barista FIRE
tiers.description: Standard, reduced by part-time income until the chosen age.

tiers.label: Coast FIRE
tiers.description: Amount needed today so that, with no further investing, it grows into the Standard target by your FIRE age.

scenarios.label: Crash just after you retire
scenarios.description: Corpus falls 30% in your first year of retirement. The biggest real-world risk.

nudges.message: NPS Tier-1 is locked until 60. It isn't in your FIRE corpus; instead 60% arrives as a lump sum at 60 and the rest as a pension.
Employer health cover ends when you retire. Buy your own family floater while you are healthy.
People depend on your income but there's no term cover.
Emergency fund is below target. Build it before increasing SIPs.
Check each loan's end date: EMIs running past your FIRE age are added to retirement expenses.
Add the PPF opening date to see whether it's accessible at your FIRE age.
Enter the surrender value, not the sum assured. Premiums belong under Expenses → Protection.
You have money left over each month that isn't invested, so it isn't in your plan yet.
Your answer is a rough estimate. Breaking down expenses improves it the most.
